Automated PR Cleanup

Thank you for contributing to opencode.

Due to the high volume of PRs from users and AI agents, we periodically close older PRs using automated criteria so maintainers can focus review time on the most active and community-supported contributions.

This PR was closed because it matched the following cleanup criteria:

- The PR was created more than 1 month ago
- The PR had fewer than 2 positive reactions
- Positive reactions are counted as thumbs-up, heart, celebration, or rocket reactions on the PR

PRs created within the last month are not affected by this cleanup.

If you believe this PR was closed incorrectly, or if you are still actively working on it, please leave a comment explaining why it should be reopened. A maintainer can review and reopen it if appropriate.

Thanks again for taking the time to contribute.

There is a workaround for that error, which is Ctrl + X > Down, enter the failed subagent , Control + P > Copy session transcript. At the beggining is the session_id, hand it to the agent and they can resume the session or read it with that.

> Actually, there's an option in OpenCode that lots of users might not know. You can set the permission `doom_loop` to `deny` to halt identical tool calls repeated 3+ consecutive times.
> 
> See https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions

Part of the problem with this is that often doom loops end up being the same 2-3 repeated calls, so it becomes a little more annoying to detect

e.g., 

```bash

<thinking> let me check X
read Y/X
<thinking> X isn't in Y, let me check Z
read Z/X
<thinking> X isn't in Z, let me check Y
read Y/X
.
.
.
```

I think another solution would be to add a hard limit to `steps` rather than soft suggestion. Or at least, a way to safeguard against failures becoming too costly

For anyone on Windows who is tired of waiting for this to land: here is a PowerShell script that builds opencode locally with this PR applied on top of **latest `dev`**. Why not just build the PR branch directly? Its head is based on an older `dev`, so building it as-is downgrades you and drops everything merged since. The script instead checks out latest `origin/dev` and 3-way merges only the files this PR touches onto it, then builds and installs the CLI and/or the Desktop app locally. **Usage** ```powershell git clone https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode.git pwsh -File .\update-opencode.ps1 # CLI + Desktop pwsh -File .\update-opencode.ps1 -Target cli # CLI only pwsh -File .\update-opencode.ps1 -DryRun # port the PR, stop before building ``` **Requirements:** PowerShell 7, `git`, `bun`. The Desktop target additionally needs Node (`npx`) and ripgrep (`rg`). Because the script overwrites the binary behind the global npm shim, run `npm i -g opencode-ai` once first; for the Desktop target, install the official Desktop app once. **Notes** - Paths auto-resolve (repo next to the script or under `~`, `%APPDATA%\npm\node_modules\opencode-ai` or `npm root -g`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\...`). Override with `-RepoPath` / `-CliNpmDir` / `-DesktopInstall`, or set `$env:OPENCODE_SOURCE`. - Reversible: the previous CLI exe is kept next to the new one as `opencode.exe.old-running-`, and the previous `app.asar` is backed up under `%TEMP%\opencode`. - Build is stamped `-pr29831` on channel `prod`, so CLI and Desktop keep sharing `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. - Install renames the running exe instead of killing it, so the session you launch it from survives; open a new terminal to pick up the new binary. Use `-ForceKillCli` if you would rather it kill the running CLI. - `-SkipPr` builds plain latest `dev` if you just want a local build without the patch. Tested on Windows 11 / PowerShell 7 against `dev` 1.18.7 (CLI and Desktop). I am not the PR author, just sharing what I have been using until this gets merged.
update-opencode.ps1 ```powershell #Requires -Version 7 <# .SYNOPSIS Windows: rebuild + install OpenCode CLI and/or Desktop from latest origin/dev with PR #29831 (detached-child shell hang fix) ported on top. channel=prod by default. .DESCRIPTION Why this exists: PR #29831 fixes the Windows hang where a shell tool call never returns because a detached child keeps the pipe open. The PR branch is based on an OLD dev, so building the PR head directly downgrades you. This script instead checks out latest origin/dev and 3-way merges only the PR's files onto it, then builds and installs locally. Pipeline (same source / channel / PR for both targets): 1) fetch origin/dev (+ the PR ref) 2) port the PR onto dev via per-file 3-way merge (git merge-file) and commit 3) bun install 4) build + install the selected targets Channel "prod" makes both targets use ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (shared sessions). Non-prod channels get opencode-.db and Desktop userData ai.opencode.desktop.. CLI install uses Windows rename-while-running so the current session can stay up; new terminals pick up the new binary. Desktop is stopped briefly to replace app.asar. REQUIREMENTS - PowerShell 7 (pwsh), git, bun - Desktop target only: npx (Node) and rg (ripgrep, for the build-marker check) - A clone of the repo: git clone https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode.git - CLI target only: opencode installed once via npm, so the launcher shim exists: npm i -g opencode-ai - Desktop target only: the official OpenCode Desktop installed once. PATHS All paths auto-resolve for the current user; nothing is hardcoded to one machine. repo : $env:OPENCODE_SOURCE, else

Here is some better information.  but first:

Before even spending time on this:  is it possible to have opencode use its builtin lsp support--in this case, clangd-lsp for c++--to navigate code semantically and find symbols, etc?  If not, then this is an issue that can't be solved.  I'll make a feature request, but it is not a big deal.

If the lsp feature does enable code navigation, then the problem may have to do with requesting incorrect tools to use and nothing to do with Serena.  My instance of opencode is not configured with ANY mcp servers, so can't be connecting to Serena.   But, the AGENTS.md for a project proposes using lsp for some navigation and search tasks--mostly intended for codex cli or kilo code.  opencode was trying to follow the "tip" with wrong tools.  I fixed this with an explicit ## OPENCODE section which explicitly said NOT to use Serena--problem gone.   But, with a more complex OPENCODE section, using lsp search was proposed for limited cases, but possibly with incorrect tool suggestions. What follows goes into that more.

Update: root-caused to OpenCode's native tool-discovery mechanism, not Serena/MCP.

Original report conflated two separate issues. Splitting them out after further investigation:

Not the cause: AGENTS.md was instructing OpenCode to use Serena MCP (a recommendation written for Codex CLI/Kilo Code compatibility). OpenCode has no Serena MCP server configured (opencode mcp list confirms zero servers registered), so there was nothing to actually fail — the model was just following a stale instruction pointing at a nonexistent tool. Fixed on my end via an OpenCode-specific AGENTS.md override; not an OpenCode bug.

Actual bug: After removing the Serena instruction, a semantic-navigation query ("find uses of X in calls to Y using the initializer_list overload") triggers OpenCode's internal tool_search mechanism, which fails with:

Missing required parameter: 'input[21].arguments'.

Model in use: GPT-5.6 Terra (OpenAI family, via Responses API).

Ruled out as external:

Global npm (npm ls -g --depth=0): only npm/corepack, nothing plugin-related
.opencode/plugin/ (both project and global): empty
Vendored node_modules next to the opencode binary: standard deps only (@ai-sdk, zod, effect, cross-spawn, etc.) — nothing named around tool-search/deferred-tools/BM25
Reproduces identically under opencode --pure (external plugins disabled)

Points to tool_search being native to core (or one of the "built-in plugins" per opencode debug v2 — haven't yet confirmed which).

Why this matters more than a normal failed-tool-call: when the earlier (misconfigured) Serena path failed, the agent recovered gracefully and fell back to ripgrep. This failure does not recover — the session hangs on the malformed call. A tool that's occasionally reached for and fails safely is a minor issue; one that hangs the session is not.

Suspected mechanism: this error string is a known signature of the OpenAI Responses API rejecting a tool call where the argument schema wasn't correctly populated — this exact failure mode (deferred/discovered tool + OpenAI-family model + empty or malformed arguments schema → input[N].arguments rejection) is independently documented in at least one unrelated OpenCode community plugin implementing a similar tool-search pattern, which explicitly calls out that non-Anthropic models need the full parameter schema preserved, not just descriptions. Worth checking whether OpenCode's own tool_search implementation has the same gap for OpenAI-family models specifically.

To reproduce:

Model: GPT-5.6 Terra
Prompt requiring semantic call-site/overload tracing (not a simple grep-able string match)
Observe tool_search invocation in the tool trace with a natural-language query
Session hangs on Missing required parameter: 'input[N].arguments'
